answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake bonded to a unique hardware-attested cipher key: spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand stakes, so an attacker pays linearly per identity while an honest agent pays once. Reputation then accrues like sediment - a new identity starts as loose shale, gaining weight only through verified useful work over time, while one that behaves well can bloom into a trusted lotus with higher limits. Misbehavior slashes the stake, so cheap identity farming stops paying.
